Subject: Productizing Redwood into partner UI — integration, branding & commercial next steps

Hi Karthik & Marissa,

Thanks again for the demo last week — the team at Nimbus is excited about embedding the model capabilities directly into our Analytics Studio UI. A few things we want to align on before we kick off a POC:

- Integration mode options: we need clarity on hosted API vs dedicated pool vs an on-prem/private option (we expect some customers will require strict data residency).
- Surface-level branding: Nimbus wants the feature to appear native in our UI (no heavy Redwood branding). We are open to a small “powered by Redwood” link in the footer; please confirm any required wording.
- Commercial models: looking at reseller margin vs rev-share vs flat per-seat SKU. Also need an estimate for upfront integration engineering hours.
- Legal: we’ll need a short MSA + IP/branding annex and standard SOC2 evidence.

Can you share a short technical spec (SDK or API integration patterns), a mutual action plan (high-level milestones), and a draft commercial term so our GTM folks can internalize? Target: start POC in Q3 (ideally Aug).

Attaching: none from our side yet — we can send product mocks if useful.

Best,

Hi Olivia — great to hear and thanks for the clear bullets. Quick summary from our side and what I can attach right away:

Integration modes (tradeoffs) — short form:
- Hosted API (fastest): Redwood-hosted models, simplest integration (HTTP + streaming). Good for experimentation and lowest TTM. Requires clear data policies; supports prefix/KV caching to reduce cost.
- Dedicated pool (reserved): predictable throughput, isolated data plane. Best for sustained production scale and lower per-token price.
- Private deployment (VPC/on-prem): for regulated customers needing full control. Longer lead time and project-based pricing.

Branding: We’re comfortable with a native UX for Nimbus. Our legal team typically requires a small “Powered by Redwood” link and a short attribution line in partner-facing docs — we’ll propose exact language in the MSA annex.

Commercial: We have three common paths — reseller margin, rev-share, or fixed SKU plus integration fee. I’ll loop Marissa for detailed commercial proposals and a sample MAP.

Next: attaching a concise SDK/Integration spec and a draft MAP to get us started. Can you share a legal contact for MSA review? Also propose a 30-minute kickoff next Tue or Wed (Aug week 2); what works for your team?

Attachments: Redwood_Partner_SDK_Spec.pdf (integration patterns + code snippets), MAP_Nimbus_v1.xlsx (draft timeline / owners)

Thanks,
Karthik
Head of Partner Integrations | Redwood Inference

Folks — quick commercial thoughts so we’re aligned before we send a formal proposal to Olivia: 

- Intro offer: 20% off list for the first 12 months or 6 months of waived integration support hours (pick one). Nimbus is mid-market with upsell potential; discount should be contingent on a 12-mo commitment and HubSpot deal stage criteria.
- Pricing model: propose two tracks to Nimbus: (A) Hosted API with per-token pricing + integrated usage dashboard (fastest), (B) Dedicated pool with committed QPS and monthly flat fee (lower unit cost). Recommend we present both and guide them.
- Rev-share: only if Nimbus signs a co-sell plan and joint GTM commitments (paid campaigns + webinar). Otherwise prefer reseller margin or fixed fee.
- SLA / Support: include S1 on-call for production customers (add-on). They will likely expect a standard 99.9% uptime target for dedicated.

I’ll turn this into a short commercial sheet after Karthik confirms the integration mode. Attaching the MAP so we can map owners to dates.

Thanks,
Marissa
Account Executive, Strategic Partnerships

Looping in legal considerations — a few items we should include in the draft MSA/annex:

1) Branding and attribution language (exact text + allowed logo lockups). Nimbus wants minimal branding; we can approve a small “Powered by Redwood” text link but require prior approval of any co-branded marketing.
2) IP & derivative data: confirm that models’ weights and Redwood core IP remain our property; clarify training/derivative model usage prohibitions.
3) Security evidence: provide SOC2 report and an onboarding checklist for customers that require additional attestations.
4) Termination & transition: add a data export/hand-off clause if Nimbus requests migration to a private deployment later.

I’ve started a draft MSA for internal review (MSA_redwood_partner_draft_v0.1.pdf). Will send to them after Marissa signs off on commercial bullets.

— Camila
